entry.text: Project Name: RappidX– GenAI-Powered Legacy Modernization
Duration: August 2024 – Present
Role: Generative AI Technical Architect & Program Lead
Responsibilities:
• Spearheading a high-impact AI modernization initiative aimed at transforming legacy enterprise
systems into an intelligent, LLM-native architecture using LangChain, LangGraph, and Graph-RAG
pipelines.
• Architected an advanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework with support for
Knowledge-Augmented Generation (KAG) and Agentic RAG to convert unstructured business
documentation into executable Python code and microservices.
• Designed a scalable Multi-Agent System (MAS) leveraging Toolformer-style agents and Autonomous AI
Systems to autonomously interpret, refactor, and generate new business logic code from legacy
codebases.
• Led the end-to-end development strategy using LLMOps best practices, integrating Prompt Engineering,
RAG Fusion, and Vector Databases (FAISS, Weaviate, Pinecone) for document chunking, semantic
retrieval, and long-context reasoning.
• Provided architectural direction for GenAI pipelines embedded with real-time decision-making
capabilities across financial, compliance, and operational workflows.
• Oversaw a cross-functional team of 45+ AI/ML engineers, architects, and DevOps professionals,
mentoring them on GenAI methodologies, performance tuning, and best practices in AI system design.
• Built a modular GenAI SDK with internal APIs and toolchains to streamline integration across services,
optimizing for scalability, accuracy, and latency.
• Championed the development of LLM-powered business logic reconstruction models, replacing brittle
rule-based engines with context-aware, auto-evolving AI code generators.
• Evangelized GenAI adoption across leadership and engineering teams, helping align AI strategy with
long-term business transformation goals.
• Utilized Docker , Redis, and PyCharm for local DevOps workflows, and deployed AI agents on
microservice-based environments for fast iteration and scalability.

entry.text: Project Objective:
To developed GenAI-driven platform to automate portfolio risk assessment, investment insight generation,
and institutional financial reporting system using custom Large Language Model (BlackRock-FinLLM).
Responsibilities:
• Designed and developed BlackRock-FinLLM, a domain-specific LLM fine-tuned on institutional financial
data, including fund performance reports, market trends, and macroeconomic indicators.
• Designed and developed BlackRock-FinLLM, a domain-specific LLM fine-tuned on institutional financial
data, including fund performance reports, market trends, and macroeconomic indicators.
• Built AI-powered portfolio risk evaluation modules leveraging transformer models (BERT , Falcon,
LLaMA, GPT-NeoX) to identify exposure anomalies, liquidity risks, and asset correlations.
• Engineered data ingestion and pretraining pipelines that processed millions of financial records from
internal databases, regulatory disclosures, and real-time market feeds for model training.
• Implemented RAG-based reporting automation, combining LangChain, LlamaIndex, and FAISS to enable
LLMs to generate context-aware financial summaries and compliance-ready reports.
• Developed LLM inference microservices using FastAPI, containerized with Docker, and deployed on
AWS Sagemaker for scalable real-time portfolio intelligence delivery.
• Created prompt-engineered templates for automated generation of quarterly fund commentaries, risk
summaries, and performance dashboards with verifiable audit trails.
• Applied parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA, PEFT) and quantization techniques to improve LLM
throughput and cost efficiency in production environments.
• Collaborated with quantitative risk teams and compliance analysts to ensure model outputs align with
financial governance, audit transparency, and institutional reporting standards.
• Established continuous model evaluation pipelines using MLflow for tracking report accuracy, risk
detection metrics, and language model drift.
Tools & Technologies: Python, FastAPI, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, LangChain, LlamaIndex,
FAISS, Docker , AWS Sagemaker, EC2, MLflow, Pandas, NumPy, LoRA, PEFT , GitHub

entry.text: Project Objective:
To automate the personal loan origination process by integrating AI-driven credit evaluation,
document understanding, and risk profiling using transformer-based NLP and backend microservices.
Responsibilities:
• Led R&D and backend development to automate personal loan applications, integrating credit bureaus
(CIBIL, Equifax, Experian) for real-time borrower credit evaluation.
• Fetching credit information from different credit beuro (CIBIL, EQUIFAX and Experian) and analysis and
assessing reports using PreTrained Distil-BERT model.
• Designed and fine-tuned BERT Base and DistilBERT models to extract and classify key financial
entities (income, liabilities, PAN/Aadhaar data) from user-submitted documents.
• Built a document intelligence pipeline combining Google OCR, BERT embeddings, and
semantic similarity models for loan processing(Loan amount and Eligibility calculating).
• Developed AI-driven creditworthiness scoring models and decision trees for FLDG lending risk
assessment, enhancing underwriting precision.
• Experimented with GPT-2 and T5 for text summarization and synthetic data generation to augment
limited labeled datasets in loan application scenarios.
• Created scalable RESTful microservices using Python (Django REST Framework) to orchestrate
document parsing, NLP inference, and credit scoring workflows.
• Conducted research on transformer explainability and feature attribution to ensure compliance
with financial transparency regulations.
• Deployed and optimized AI models on AWS EC2 and Lambda, reducing response latency by over
40% for real-time credit assessments.
• Collaborated with cross-functional data and credit teams to align ML model outcomes with business
rules and improve loan approval accuracy.
Tools & Technologies: Python, Django REST Framework, BERT Base, DistilBERT , GPT-2, T5, Hugging Face
Transformers, AWS EC2, Lambda, Google OCR, Pandas, NumPy, Postman, GitHub
